title: M1: Prove the private KWin stack and record the dependency baseline
outcome: A reproducible, bounded compatibility harness proves the proposed platform adapters on the target Arch Linux/KDE Wayland machine before their interfaces are committed to production.
scope: Record target package/native-library versions, exact source revisions, resolved Python environment, maintained patches, and setup steps; evaluate the proposed kdotool revision.
Run an owner-private bus and headless KWin at 1280×720 scale 1 inside a transient user service with bounded cleanup and durable diagnostic output.

Build a minimal deterministic native Wayland custom-rendered fixture with input acknowledgments and controllable visual state for the initial window/input/capture probes; this fixture is reusable by production adapter tests.

Probe structured custom-rendered window queries and verified focus using kdotool, resumed EIS/libei devices and acknowledged input using project-owned bindings, and fresh ScreenShot2 capture with concurrent pipe draining.
Record measurements and choose finite proposed startup, query, action, cancellation, capture and shutdown limits; record blockers and evidence-based design changes.
acceptance: A checked-in harness and evidence demonstrate all three adapters in the intended private service environment without prompts or touching the host desktop.
The limited ctypes surface is checked against supported libei headers, including void ei_dispatch and event/object ownership; input correctness defects are resolved before that adapter passes.
Setup is reproducible from recorded versions and any patches; missing capabilities produce actionable failures. Each failed probe cleans up its owned processes within a recorded bound.

An architecture decision records go/no-go for kdotool, Python/libei, capture isolation and the GLib loop. A blocker prevents dependent production integration until resolved; prototype results are explicitly not a support claim.
exclusions: Do not install, invoke, vendor or patch ydotool or kwin-mcp. No MCP SDK, viewer, XWayland, alternate backend framework, or support claim.

title: M2: Establish the CLI, generation-safe protocol, and durable records
outcome: The Python CLI and persistent-worker contract provide predictable machine-readable results, identity checks, caller-relative paths, finite deadlines and durable diagnostics.
scope: Package agent-desktop with explicit flags/defaults and all documented command families; commands not yet wired fail explicitly rather than reporting success.
Define a versioned owner-only Unix-socket JSON protocol with request IDs, generation-scoped handles, structured errors and meaningful exit status, including parser failures.
Implement request admission, monotonic deadlines including queue time, single ordinary-action serialization and responsive cancellation/reset/stop control handling.
Define generation-specific durable artifacts, atomic manifests, correlated logs, caller path normalization, executable/PATH and environment precedence; record headless mode.
acceptance: Separate CLI processes exchange requests with a persistent worker; JSON stdout contains one result only, including errors, and subprocess/application logs stay separate.
Every session-addressed command accepts an expected generation and checks it before side effects; name-only resolution and non-retry semantics are documented.

Queue delay consumes the timeout; SIGINT and socket loss reach active work without queueing, while required cleanup survives client exit. Test task doubles can establish this infrastructure before real adapters arrive.

Artifact paths are caller-relative, generation-specific and collision-free; manifests retain required provenance and outcomes without dumping secrets. Failures identify partial/uncertain effects and retain available application handles.
exclusions: No persistent project configuration format or exactly-once execution claim; real desktop acceptance remains in later milestones.

title: M3: Own private sessions with bounded supervision and cleanup
outcome: A generation-bound systemd service owns the worker, private desktop and ordinary descendants, with reliable failure detection and an independent cleanup path.
scope: Implement per-name lifecycle locking, generation-specific unit/runtime ownership, duplicate-start compatibility and idempotent stop.
Create owner-only runtime and disposable HOME/XDG settings; construct explicit private Wayland/D-Bus endpoints and reject protected overrides, stripping host display and accessibility endpoints.
Supervise private bus and KWin; use no automatic restart, KillMode=control-group, finite TimeoutStopSec and a bounded terminal-record/runtime cleanup hook.
Implement capability-based readiness using the M1 probe interfaces until production adapters are connected, live status and independent worker/compositor/bus failure detection.
Provide graceful-shutdown hooks for action cancellation, release and application close, followed by bounded service-manager fallback even with an unresponsive worker.
acceptance: Sessions survive separate CLI invocations and only become ready after control, window, resumed input and screenshot probes all pass; failed startup retains diagnostics and cleans up.
Duplicate starts return the compatible generation or reject conflict. Stale-generation commands, including fallback stop and cleanup hooks, cannot affect a replacement session.
Independent death or unresponsiveness tests cover worker, compositor and bus; status rejects work after essential failure and cgroup cleanup removes ordinary descendants within the deadline.

Private socket/files have owner-only access; trusted applications keep project/network access while receiving only intended desktop/settings endpoints. Durable artifacts and failure outcomes survive cleanup.
exclusions: No security sandbox or support for deliberately escaping supervision. Production release/reset/close hooks and readiness are completed and tested in M7.

title: M4: Launch owned applications and control windows by verified identity
outcome: One native Wayland application and its dialogs can be launched, discovered, focused, waited on, closed or explicitly terminated with generation and process-ownership checks.
scope: Launch argv without an implicit shell, using normalized cwd and documented final PATH/env; retain application/process identity, logs, descendants and exit state even after timeout or cancellation.
Implement an asynchronously observed pinned kdotool adapter and fixed safely parameterized query for KWin identity, PID, title/class, client/frame geometry and focus.
Select by explicit window identity or unambiguous owned-application association; expose candidates and null/unavailable metadata; validate again after queue delay.
Implement bounded focus/window/exit waits, graceful selected-window close without automatic dialog handling or signaling, and separate owned-process termination.
Extend the M1 fixture with dialogs, duplicate titles, delayed window creation, exits and descendants while implementing application/window behavior.
acceptance: Real custom-rendered fixture windows and dialogs are discovered without accessibility; identical titles never substitute for identity and ambiguous or vanished targets fail clearly.
Focus succeeds only after the requested window is observed active; waits distinguish exit, timeout, cancellation and session failure.
Timed-out window waits retain application handles. PID-reuse simulation and real descendant tests show termination signals only verified owned processes and reports remaining processes.
Relative executable/cwd/output paths work from a different caller directory; confirmation dialogs remain available for explicit interaction, and close timeout sends no termination signal.
exclusions: No multiple active applications, title-based guessing, implicit shell, accessibility automation, or automatic confirmation dismissal.

title: M5: Deliver targeted input with bounded cancellation and recovery
outcome: Keyboard and pointer actions use verified window focus, finite sequences, tracked releases and an event-responsive private libei connection.
scope: Implement the minimal header-verified ctypes/libei binding and one GLib execution context for device events and emission; require usable resumed devices and process pause/removal/disconnect continuously.
Prevalidate physical keys, finite holds, complete chords and the documented US-layout text set before input; track generated modifiers as well as explicit keys/buttons.
Require a window for every input action, recheck current existence/focus/geometry and translate bounded client coordinates excluding decorations.
Run cancellable short steps with bounded focus rechecks; cancel on target/focus/device loss, SIGINT, disconnect or deadline, including delayed desktop queries.
Attempt release on all outcomes; expose uncertainty and block further input until successful reset or stop. Reset cancels active work and restores a usable connection without replay.
Extend the existing fixture and harness with focus theft, modified-text/hold acknowledgments and controlled input-device fault scenarios as each behavior is implemented.
acceptance: The real instrumented app acknowledges supported text, chords, common game keys, finite holds/releases and content-coordinate clicks; unsupported full requests emit no input.
Focus theft, vanished targets, slow/timed-out focus queries, queued actions, modified typing and held input satisfy measured polling/cancellation/release bounds.
Device pause, removal and connection loss stop emission, report readiness/uncertainty accurately and require a successful reset where release is uncertain; reset failure leaves input unavailable.
Cancellation/reset/stop bypass the ordinary queue and never concurrently manipulate libei. Results explicitly describe dispatch, without implying application acknowledgment or frame readiness.
exclusions: No indefinite key-down across commands, Unicode/IME, richer pointer actions or atomic compositor-level window targeting promise.

title: M6: Capture fresh complete screenshots and preserve useful artifacts
outcome: The CLI captures the whole private output as a newly written PNG while cancellation and health monitoring remain responsive, and exposes durable correlated artifacts.
scope: Implement the direct private ScreenShot2 D-Bus adapter with concurrent pipe drain, validated metadata/pixel format, finite deadlines and owned descriptor/subprocess cleanup.
Keep blocking capture work outside the control loop using the boundary validated in M1; encode with Pillow, write a unique temporary artifact and publish only a complete PNG.
Return generation, absolute path, dimensions, capture timestamp and backend; wire logs/artifact discovery and complete manifests for requests, launches, dependency provenance and terminal outcomes.
acceptance: Real capture without a viewer yields a fresh complete 1280×720 PNG per request; after fixture acknowledgment a changed rendering is visible and prior images are never reused as fresh output.

Slow/hung capture, partial reads, unsupported formats, write failures, cancellation and private-bus loss fail with stable context, leak no owned resources and cannot publish partial files as successes.

Capture cannot block cancellation, stop or health processing; screenshots/logs/manifest survive failed startup and cleanup, concurrent filename allocation does not collide, and JSON stdout remains clean.
exclusions: No viewer, window-specific capture, generic rendered-frame readiness promise or second capture backend without demonstrated need.

title: M7: Integrate the complete workflow and verify failure contracts
outcome: Production adapters are connected to readiness, shutdown and every CLI command; a real-desktop integration suite demonstrates the full normal and failure workflows.
scope: Replace preliminary probes/hooks with production window/input/capture/app integrations and finalize doctor capability reporting and stable error mapping.
Assemble the fixtures built in M1/M4/M5 into the complete integration harness, adding controlled process failures and delays where needed; do not defer adapter-critical fixtures to this milestone.
Exercise separate CLI processes through launch, discover, focus, capture, type, hold/release, click, close and stop, with application acknowledgment before pixel assertions.
Automate the complete REQ-038 matrix plus duplicate/conflicting start, close timeout, explicit kill, queued deadline expiry, failed reset, capture failure and worker-hang fallback.
Measure and enforce documented timing limits under slow queries/capture and ensure required cleanup remains independent of clients.
acceptance: All required command families operate noninteractively against the real private KWin service; complete startup readiness uses production adapters and shutdown attempts actual release and graceful close before fallback.
Every REQ-038 condition has an identified test and retained diagnostic evidence; missing required platform capabilities fail the support gate rather than silently passing or being skipped.

Tests establish stale-generation protection before side effects (including start/stop races), no host endpoint fallback, no PID-reuse signaling, bounded descendant cleanup and durable terminal manifests for independent essential-process deaths.

Actual cancellation/focus-polling/deadline measurements meet the published bounds, including slow desktop calls, client disappearance, modified typing and held input. Uncertain effects are exposed without retries.
exclusions: Mocks may supplement edge cases but cannot replace real-compositor workflow and device-lifecycle evidence. This milestone does not itself satisfy the twenty-run support gate.

title: M8: Qualify the first supported release and publish reproducible workflows
outcome: A recorded target environment passes twenty consecutive full workflows and users have reproducible setup, smoke checks and precise support boundaries.
scope: Document setup and pinned/resolved dependencies, CLI JSON workflow, caller path/environment behavior, generation handling, supported input mappings, timing/cancellation/reset and troubleshooting.
Run the complete CLI workflow twenty consecutive times against the recorded target environment, preserving per-run outcomes and checking prompts, stuck input and remaining owned processes.
Choose and record a representative native Wayland application or game relevant to the user's workflow in addition to the fixture, or explicitly document a reasoned REQ-044 exception.
Publish a requirement-to-implementation/test index and evidence, identify supported versions/apps and deferred capabilities, and document affected compatibility checks required on dependency changes.
acceptance: Twenty consecutive runs pass without unexpected prompts, stuck input or leftover owned processes; any failure is retained and the consecutive count restarts after fixes.
All MUST requirements have passing evidence, including M7's failure suite; relevant checks are rerun after dependency or implementation changes affecting those results.
A clean setup and documented smoke command reproduce the workflow; timing limits state tested conditions, and input dispatch is distinguished from app acknowledgment/rendering.
Support claims name only recorded tested environments/applications. All SHOULD requirements are addressed or carry documented exceptions and consequences; optional MAY features remain deferred.
exclusions: No general game compatibility, filesystem/network sandboxing, concurrent automation clients, cross-distribution support, live viewing, X11 or MCP delivery commitment.
